named_confounds: genre composition change (early period small, juvenile-heavy late)
sparse early cells (37-165 works per genre before 1876)
rationale: Data: 6766 works, one passage each (rate = binary DISTANCE_TRAVEL flag), years 1800-1925, cutoff 1876; only 752 works fall before it. Estimand: work-level rates averaged equally within each genre x period cell, then late-minus-early differences averaged equally across 8 genres. Result +0.025 (2.5 percentage points); 95% CI from a bootstrap stratified by genre x period is [0.002, 0.045], and an author-cluster bootstrap gives a similar [0.001, 0.048]. Six of eight genres go up (romance 0 to 0.059, collection 0.027 to 0.102, juvenile 0.118 to 0.160); adventure and sensation dip slightly. The sign stays positive for cutoffs from 1850 to 1900 (0.009 to 0.045), and the decade means rise from about 0.03-0.07 before 1850 to about 0.11 after 1890. Fragility: keeping only medium or high date confidence gives 0.020 [-0.005, 0.048]; high only gives 0.015 [-0.026, 0.052]; known origin only gives 0.025 [-0.015, 0.057]. Single-edition works give 0.032 [0.008, 0.051], and passage-confidence filtering changes nothing. So the increase is consistent in direction, but its significance is marginal and depends on including works with uncertain dates. Other explanations: small early cells; changes in what gets sampled or digitized within genres; dating errors moving works across the cutoff; drift in how passages were labeled. The cited passage IDs are tagged DISTANCE_TRAVEL and only illustrate the construct; they do not prove a trend. Confidence is moderate.
